author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Vita3K makes guest memory writes invalidate Vulkan surfaces
summary: Protected backing ranges now mark cached color surfaces dirty, preventing stale GPU images from being reused as textures after the CPU changes their memory.
heroAlt: Source evidence from Vita3K pull request #3758: renderer/vulkan: Add dirty flag to surface cache

sourceLabels.vita3k-pr-3758: renderer/vulkan: Add dirty flag to surface cache

blocks.text: A surface can exist in GPU memory after the guest changes its backing bytes

Vita3K caches Vita color surfaces as Vulkan resources. When a game writes the corresponding guest memory from the CPU, the cached image may no longer represent that address range. Returning it as a texture can show an old frame or effect. Some linear formats also require GPU-to-guest synchronization when the CPU reads them, so read and write faults have related but different meanings.
Protection callbacks now carry shared sync and dirty state

Pull request #3758 gives each ColorSurfaceCacheInfo a shared dirty flag. protect_surface aligns the safely protectable interior to 4 KiB pages. Sync-capable linear surfaces use MemPerm::None to trap reads and writes and capture need_surface_sync; other surfaces use ReadOnly to trap writes. A write marks dirty. For a surface smaller than a page, dirty tracking is withheld because unrelated data on the same protected page would create false invalidations.
Cache lookup refuses GPU data after a CPU write

When a color surface is requested as a texture, a set dirty flag returns no cached result, forcing the caller away from stale GPU content. When the same surface becomes a framebuffer again, Vita3K can rearm protection and clear dirty after establishing the new authoritative use. Overlapping protections combine through most_restrictive_perm so adding a weaker range cannot accidentally reopen memory already guarded more strongly.
Memory mapping methods and page overlap are key tests

Render to a surface, sample it, rewrite all or part from the guest CPU, then sample again for linear and tiled formats. Include aligned, unaligned, sub-page, overlapping, and shared-page allocations; confirm small surfaces avoid false dirty flags without hiding real changes. Test readback synchronization separately from write invalidation. Repeat on native buffer mapping, double buffering, NVIDIA and non-NVIDIA Linux drivers, Android, and savestate restore. Record protection faults to catch loops or excessive hot-path trapping.
A cache is correct only while its ownership evidence is current; one guest write is enough to revoke the GPU surface's claim to that memory.
